name: performance

findings.message: Every cycle iteration now performs two `locked_state_update` calls (one added at iter-start, one pre-existing at iter-end), each involving flock acquisition, a `jq empty` validation subprocess, a jq transform subprocess, mktemp, and an atomic rename — doubling per-iteration blocking I/O on the cycle hot path.
findings.quote:
_cycle_state_write_iter_start "$state_file" "$cycle_id" "$iter" \
            || warn "cycle-orchestrator: failed to write iter-start state for cycle=$cycle_id iter=$iter (a resume may start at the wrong iteration)"

findings.message: On the resume startup path, every complete dispatch unit triggers `get_state_field` inside a subshell `$(...)`, spawning a `jq empty` validation subprocess plus a `jq` extraction subprocess per stage — O(N) subprocess pairs where N is the number of completed stages.

In `_cycle_iter_dispatch` on the first resumed iteration, each complete cycle member spawns four separate `jq` subprocesses (status read, verdict read, blob-entry construction, blob merge) that could be collapsed into a single `jq` call reading all three fields at once.
